threads.body: [Testing] This suite discovers both `PulsarClientTest` from `src/test/java` and `PulsarClientV5Test`; because both extend `AbstractPulsarClientTest`, JUnit runs the four inherited tests twice and starts a separate Pulsar broker for each class. This adds a costly duplicate container/test cycle. Consider making the v5 class extend `PulsarClientTest` and filtering this suite to execute only that subclass, so it inherits the legacy coverage and adds the v5 cases in one fixture lifecycle.

replies.body:
Addressed in da855574e07afcad14ae84c525b8ad831a6db251.

The frozen suite compiled src/test/java and src/version5Test/java and excluded only the suppression class, selecting both PulsarClientTest and PulsarClientV5Test. Both inherited four base tests and the broker lifecycle. Candidate commit 1 selects only PulsarClientV5Test, now extending PulsarClientTest, so it retains every legacy test and the synchronous/asynchronous v5 cases while using one inherited fixture lifecycle. Actual JUnit dry-run reports contain exactly that subclass and every inherited method once.
